{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-or-c","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"b6bd0c8743f1fa1ee69c4f89e57fd80697585ce03990d15d7e90fac4fa0283bb","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-or-class-c:lineage:37","source_registry_sha256":"ce8335c1d96ff7ed209bf236ba9a56fe92dfebd915bc0e2fa7fb830ee03f0f09","source_liveness_sha256":"c4da479589e7933e4eef7366086dfcc48a420303d0089cb0ea19ad9137abec1d"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C2"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Safe and responsible driving: defensive driving, restraints, collision avoidance, lights, night and bad-weather driving","heading":"C2 — Snow, ice, skids and traction devices plus confusables: low versus high beams, dimming distances, skid steering and chains versus traction tires","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 — Snow, ice, skids and traction devices plus confusables: low versus high beams, dimming distances, skid steering and chains versus traction tires
Continuation facts for the snow, ice, skid and traction pages followed by confusable pairs, each tied to one manual page; knowledge-graph hints (group, difficulty, confusable pair) sit only in the trailing Why it matters line of each block.

FACT_ID: sec09-R01 | anchor: A06
Follow weather forecasts and warnings, and stay off the road when police or highway officials say driving is very hazardous. [A06]
Why it matters: group snow and ice; continuation; difficulty easy.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec09-R02 | anchor: A06
On snow or ice, press the gas pedal gently, because too much power can spin the tires or slide the vehicle. [A06]
Why it matters: group snow and ice; continuation; difficulty easy.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec09-R03 | anchor: A06
On snow or ice, press and release the brakes gently, since slamming them will likely send the vehicle into a skid. [A06]
Why it matters: group snow and ice; continuation; difficulty medium.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec09-R04 | anchor: A06
When you start out on snow or ice, get the feel of the road away from traffic and test the brakes lightly so you know how they will respond. [A06]
Why it matters: group snow and ice; continuation; difficulty easy.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec09-R05 | anchor: A06
Take turns on snow or ice at a reduced, steady speed to avoid skidding. [A06]
Why it matters: group snow and ice; continuation; difficulty easy.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec09-R06 | anchor: A06
Bridges and shaded spots freeze first and can be icy while the rest of the road is clear. [A06]
Why it matters: group snow and ice; continuation; difficulty medium.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec09-R07 | anchor: A06
Climbing a snowy or icy hill, give the vehicle just enough power to keep moving without spinning the wheels. [A06]
Why it matters: group snow and ice; continuation; difficulty medium.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec09-R08 | anchor: A06
A road is likely to be most slippery when the temperature is close to freezing, more so than when it is well below freezing. [A06]
Why it matters: group snow and ice; confusable near freezing versus below freezing; difficulty hard.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec09-R09 | anchor: A07
A skid happens when the tires can no longer grip the road, and driving too fast for conditions is what causes it. [A07]
Why it matters: group skids; continuation; difficulty easy.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec09-R10 | anchor: A07
In a skid, stay off the brakes, because they will not work well until the vehicle slows. [A07]
Why it matters: group skids; continuation; difficulty medium.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec09-R11 | anchor: A07
In a skid, steer the way you want the vehicle to go, turn the wheel back as soon as it starts to straighten so it does not swing the other way, and keep correcting left and right until you are back in control. [A07]
Why it matters: group skids; continuation; difficulty hard.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec09-R12 | anchor: A07
Signs may require you to carry or to use chains or traction tires. [A07]
Why it matters: group traction devices; continuation; difficulty easy.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec09-R13 | anchor: A07
In Oregon, chains include link chains, cable chains and any other device fastened to the wheel, the vehicle or the outside of the tire that is built to add traction on snow and ice. [A07]
Why it matters: group traction devices; confusable chains versus traction tires; difficulty medium.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec09-R14 | anchor: A07
Traction tires are studded tires, retractable studded tires or tires that meet the tire industry definition for severe snow use, which carry a mountain and snowflake emblem on the sidewall. [A07]
Why it matters: group traction devices; confusable chains versus traction tires; difficulty medium.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec09-R15 | anchor: A07
Studded tires are generally allowed in Oregon only from November 1 through March 31, and because studs damage roads, drivers are urged to use chains or other traction tires instead. [A07]
Why it matters: group traction devices; continuation; difficulty hard.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec09-R16 | anchor: A07
Chain and traction tire requirements are published by ODOT on TripCheck.com. [A07]
Why it matters: group traction devices; continuation; difficulty easy.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec09-R17 | anchor: A04
High beams must be dimmed at 500 feet for an oncoming vehicle but at 350 feet when you are following a vehicle. [A04]
Why it matters: group headlights; confusable oncoming versus following distance; difficulty hard.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec09-R18 | anchor: A04
The 1,000-foot visibility test decides when headlights must be on beyond the sunset-to-sunrise rule, while the 500-foot and 350-foot distances decide when high beams must be dimmed. [A04]
Why it matters: group headlights; confusable lights-on distance versus dimming distance; difficulty hard.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec09-R19 | anchor: A05
In fog, dust or smoke you use low beams, not high beams, even though high beams seem brighter, because their light bounces back as glare. [A05]
Why it matters: group low visibility; confusable low beams versus high beams; difficulty medium.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec09-R20 | anchor: A02
Turning away is usually the quickest escape because most vehicles turn faster than they stop, while speeding up is the choice when the threat comes from the side or behind. [A02]
Why it matters: group collision avoidance; confusable turning versus speeding up; difficulty medium.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec09-R21 | anchor: A03
For a vehicle drifting toward you, you move right and warn it, while for a frightened animal you stop and stay quiet rather than honking. [A03]
Why it matters: group hazards; confusable drifting vehicle versus frightened animal; difficulty medium.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0083]
